summary: Story correctly decomposes the section 16 camera feel into two independently testable, independently shippable leaves, each with one behavior and two changed responsibilities (under the three-responsibility limit) and a strict subset of the parent subsystem: WI-06d-c-a owns the single flag-gated low-frequency shake path, the gate, the amplitude budget and the presentation flag; WI-06d-c-b owns the widescreen layout params and the camera-transform composition seam. Both parent criteria are retained verbatim (AC-shake-rules in c-a, AC-widescreen in c-b); their union covers the story, and their child-local status with respect to WI-06d is documented consistently in WI-06d/plan.md. Dependencies are sound: the story and both children depend on WI-06a/b/c (existing ST-06 leaves); c-a additionally depends on WI-06d-b4 for its final flag-on/off browser proof, a cross-story leaf with no cycle (b4 depends only on WI-06a/b/c and its own spec defers the flag-to-shake integration proof to this story). Each criterion has exactly one named final proof owner with focused evidence: c-a proves flag on = low-frequency shake within the section 16 budget using the b4 distant-motion impulse and flag off = no shake from any source (plus Node tests for flag plumbing, gate, budget); c-b proves composition holds at a wide aspect ratio with no letterboxed dead zones (plus Node tests for layout params and unchanged baseline framing). Section 16's offscreen-aggro fairness clause is an AI/gameplay property explicitly excluded here, and WI-06g's downstream consumption of the flag matches its existing WI-06d dependency. Handoffs let a fresh implementer proceed from the children alone.
